```{python}
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
import requests
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
```

## Data
The dataset used for this project comes from the Government of Ontario. It was sourced from the Data Catologue and can be found [here](https://data.ontario.ca/dataset/bridge-conditions).

```{python}
# create data folders if they don't exist
os.makedirs("../data/raw", exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs("../data/processed", exist_ok=True)

# download data
url = "https://data.ontario.ca/datastore/dump/703cdf01-ff09-4b86-b017-6e8d87b11fd2?bom=True"

# Write to file
request = requests.get(url)
with open("../data/raw/bridge_data_raw.csv", 'wb') as f:
    f.write(request.content)

# Load the raw data
raw_df = pd.read_csv('../data/raw/bridge_data_raw.csv')

# Filter for Bridges only
processed_df = raw_df[raw_df['CATEGORY'] == 'Bridge']

# Rename to use snake case for consistency
rename_map = {
    "ID (SITE Ndeg)": "site_id",
    "STRUCTURE NAME": "structure_name",
    "FRENCH NAME": "french_name",
    "HIGHWAY NAME": "highway_name",
    "LATITUDE": "latitude",
    "LONGITUDE": "longitude",
    "CATEGORY": "category",
    "SUBCATEGORY 1": "subcategory",
    "TYPE 1": "structure_type",
    "MATERIAL 1": "material",
    "YEAR BUILT": "year_built",
    "LAST MAJOR REHAB": "last_major_rehab",
    "LAST MINOR REHAB": "last_minor_rehab",
    "NUMBER OF SPAN / CELLS": "num_spans_cells",
    "SPAN DETAILS (m)": "span_details_m",
    "DECK / CULVERTS LENGTH (m)": "length_m",
    "WIDTH TOTAL (m)": "width_m",
    "REGION": "region",
    "COUNTY": "county",
    "OPERATION STATUS": "operation_status",
    "OWNER": "owner",
    "LAST INSPECTION DATE": "last_inspection_date",
    "CURRENT BCI": "current_bci",
}

processed_df = processed_df.rename(columns=rename_map)

# Drop rows that don't have a CURRENT_BCI (target), 52 rows
processed_df = processed_df.dropna(subset=['current_bci'])

# Create target variable
processed_df['rehab_soon'] = (processed_df['current_bci'] < 70).astype(int)

# Parse span_details_m into total, count, max, mean, and std
def extract_span_summary(val):
    """Helper function to parse span details into total,
    count, max, mean, and std span
    """
    txt = str(val).strip()
    t_match = re.search(r"Total\s*=\s*([+-]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", txt, re.IGNORECASE)
    spans = [
        float(m.group(2))
        for m in re.finditer(r"\(\s*(\d+)\s*\)\s*=\s*([+-]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", txt)
    ]

    if spans:
        arr = np.array(spans, dtype=float)
        total_val = (
            float(t_match.group(1))
            if t_match and float(t_match.group(1)) > 0
            else float(arr.sum())
        )
        return pd.Series(
            [total_val, float(len(arr)), float(arr.max()), float(arr.mean()), float(arr.std(ddof=0))]
        )

    try:
        num = float(txt.rstrip("mM "))
        return pd.Series([num, 1.0, num, num, 0.0])
    except ValueError:
        total_val = float(t_match.group(1)) if t_match else np.nan
        return pd.Series([total_val, 0.0, np.nan, np.nan, np.nan])


processed_df[['span_total_m', 'span_count', 'span_max_m', 'span_mean_m', 'span_std_m']] = (
    processed_df['span_details_m'].apply(extract_span_summary)
)

# Group together materials
low_count_materials = [
    'Unknown',
    'Engineered Wood (Psl, etc.)',
    'Mass Concrete',
    'Plastic/Geogrid/Geocell',
    'Glue Laminated Wood',
    'Masonry/Block/Rock'
]
processed_df['material'] = processed_df['material'].replace(low_count_materials, 'Other')

# Feature Engineering
processed_df['age'] = 2020 - processed_df['year_built']

processed_df['years_since_last_rehab_major'] = 2020 - processed_df['last_major_rehab'].fillna(processed_df['year_built'])
processed_df['years_since_last_rehab_minor'] = 2020 - processed_df['last_minor_rehab'].fillna(processed_df['year_built'])


# Columns to drop
drop_columns = [
    'category',
    '_id',
    'site_id',
    'structure_name',
    'french_name',
    'highway_name',
    'latitude',
    'longitude',
    '2020', '2019', '2018', '2017', '2016', '2015', '2014', '2013', '2012',
    '2011', '2010', '2009', '2008', '2007', '2006', '2005', '2004', '2003',
    '2002', '2001', '2000',
    'year_built',
    'last_major_rehab',
    'last_minor_rehab',
    'num_spans_cells',
    'span_details_m',
    'last_inspection_date'
]
processed_df = processed_df.drop(columns=drop_columns)
# Save the processed dataframe
processed_df.to_csv('../data/processed/bridge_data_processed.csv', index=False)
```

```{python}
# Split the data into training (70%) and test (30%) sets
train_df, test_df = train_test_split(
    processed_df, train_size=0.70, stratify=processed_df["rehab_soon"], random_state=522
)

train_df.to_csv("../data/processed/train_df.csv", index=False)
test_df.to_csv("../data/processed/test_df.csv", index=False)
```

Table 1: Number and proportion of bridges in the training data that need rehabilitation soon (BCI below 70).
```{python}
# EDA Summary Tables
# Make Table 1 which shows how many bridges in the training data need rehab, and how many don't.
table_1 = train_df["rehab_soon"].value_counts().sort_index().to_frame()
table_1["Proportion"] = (table_1["count"] / len(train_df)).round(2)

table_1.index = ["No", "Yes"]
table_1.index.name = "Needs rehabilitation soon"
table_1.columns = ["Number of bridges", "Proportions"]

table_1
```

Table 2: Avergage age, years since last major rehab, and size of bridges in the training data that, by whether they need rehabilitation soon.
```{python}
# Make Table 2 which shows if bridges that need rehabilitation are different from ones that don't in age, time since last rehab, and size.
table_2 = train_df.groupby("rehab_soon")[["age", "years_since_last_rehab_major", "width_m", "length_m"]].mean().round(1)

table_2.index = ["No", "Yes"]
table_2.index.name = "Needs rehabilitation soon"
table_2.columns = ["Age (years)", "Years since last major rehab", "Width (m)", "Length (m)"]


table_2
```

Figure 1: Distribution of Ontario bridge age by rehabilitation need in the training data.

```{python}
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
train_df = pd.read_csv("DSCI-522-Group-7/data/processed/train_df.csv")
age_plot = alt.Chart(train_df).mark_boxplot().encode(
    x=alt.X(
        "rehab_soon:N",
        title="Rehabilitation Status",
        axis=alt.Axis(
            labelExpr="datum.value == 0 ? 'No Rehab ' : 'Rehab Needed'",
            labelAngle=0
        )
    ),
    y=alt.Y(
        "age:Q",
        title="Bridge Age"
    )
).properties(
    title="Ontario Bridge Rehabilitation Needs",
    width=450,
    height=300
)

age_plot
```




Figure 2: Percentage of Ontario bridges requiring rehabilitation among the five most common construction materials in the training data.

```{python}
# Select the 5 most common bridge materials
top_materials = train_df["material"].value_counts().head(5).index
material_df = train_df[train_df["material"].isin(top_materials)].copy()

# Shorten material names for the graph
material_df["material_short"] = material_df["material"].replace({
    "Reinforced Cast-In-Place Concrete": "Reinforced",
    "Prestressed Precast Concrete": "Prestressed",
    "Post-Tensioned Cast-In-Place Concrete": "Post-Tensioned"
})

# Create Figure 2
material_plot = alt.Chart(material_df).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X(
        "mean(rehab_soon):Q",
        title="Bridges Needing Rehabilitation",
        axis=alt.Axis(format=".0%")
    ),
    y=alt.Y(
        "material_short:N",
        title="Concrete Material",
        sort="-x"
    ),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("material:N", title="Full Material Name"),
        alt.Tooltip(
            "mean(rehab_soon):Q",
            title="Rehabilitation Rate",
            format=".1%"
        ),
        alt.Tooltip("count():Q", title="Number of Bridges")
    ]
).properties(
    title="Ontario Bridge Rehabilitation Needs by Material",
    width=450,
    height=250
)

material_plot
```







Figure 3: Distribution of bridge lengths by rehabilitation status for Ontario bridges up to 300 metres, using training data.

```{python}
# Prepare bridge length data
length_df = train_df[["length_m", "rehab_soon"]].dropna().copy()

length_df = length_df[
    (length_df["length_m"] > 0) &
    (length_df["length_m"] <= 300)
]

length_df["Rehabilitation Status"] = length_df["rehab_soon"].map({
    0: "No Rehab Needed",
    1: "Rehab Needed"
})

# Create Figure 3: Violin plot
violin_plot = alt.Chart(length_df).transform_density(
    "length_m",
    as_=["Bridge Length", "Density"],
    groupby=["Rehabilitation Status"]
).mark_area(orient="horizontal").encode(
    x=alt.X(
        "Density:Q",
        stack="center",
        axis=None,
        title=None
    ),
    y=alt.Y(
        "Bridge Length:Q",
        title="Bridge Length (m)"
    ),
    column=alt.Column(
        "Rehabilitation Status:N",
        title=None
    ),
    color=alt.Color(
        "Rehabilitation Status:N",
        legend=None
    )
).properties(
    title=  "Ontario Bridge Length's Rehabilitation Status",


    width=200,
    height=350
)

violin_plot
```





Figure 4: Density distribution of Bridge Condition Index (BCI) for all Ontario bridges in the training data. The dashed line at BCI = 70 indicates the rehabilitation threshold.

```{python}
# Create Figure 4: BCI density distribution
bci_density = alt.Chart(train_df).transform_density(
    "current_bci",
    as_=["BCI", "Density"]
).mark_area(
    color="#929292",
    opacity=0.6,
    line={"color": "#333333"}
).encode(
    x=alt.X(
        "BCI:Q",
        title="Bridge Condition Index (BCI)",
        axis=alt.Axis(values=[0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]),
        scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, 100])
    ),
    y=alt.Y(
        "Density:Q",
        title="Density"
    )
)

# Add rehabilitation threshold at BCI = 70
threshold = alt.Chart(
    pd.DataFrame({"BCI": [70]})
).mark_rule(
    color="#333333",
    strokeDash=[6, 4],
    strokeWidth=2
).encode(
    x="BCI:Q"
)

# Combine density plot and threshold
bci_plot = (bci_density + threshold).properties(
    title="Ontario Bridge Condition Index Distribution",
    width=550,
    height=300
)

bci_plot
```
